hook.line: Half of friendly conversation is 'me too' and 'me neither'. Get them right and people feel you're on their side.
hook.en:
I don't work on Mondays.
Me neither!

examples.es:
Vivo en el centro.
Yo también.

examples.en:
I don't speak English.
Me neither.

I don't have a plan.
Me neither.
Vale cooks, and so does Tomás.

rule:
Look at the first sentence. Is it a yes-sentence or a no-sentence?

Yes-sentence (*Vivo en el centro*): agree with *también*. *Yo también* = me too.
No-sentence (*No hablo inglés*): agree with *tampoco*. *Yo tampoco* = me neither.

English lets you say 'me too' to almost anything. Spanish doesn't: *también* after a no-sentence sounds like you're disagreeing.

You can swap *yo* for anyone: *Tomás también*, *Vale tampoco*.
You can also put the word in front of a verb: *Yo también trabajo aquí. Yo tampoco leo el correo.*

To disagree, flip it:
*No tengo plan.*
*Yo sí.*

*Estoy nervioso.*
*Yo no.*

One exception you'll meet soon: after *me gusta*, Spanish answers with a different little phrase (*a mí también*). With every other verb, *yo también* and *yo tampoco* work.
smallPrint: *También* and *tampoco* are adverbs of affirmation and negation.
soundTip: *Tampoco* is *tam-PO-co*; *también* is *tam-BIÉN*, with the stress on the end.

readAndPick.es:
Trabajo en una oficina.
Yo también.
options: The second person works in an office too.
The second person doesn't work in an office.

readAndPick.es:
No leo el correo.
Yo tampoco.
options: The second person reads the email.
The second person doesn't read the email either.
The second person isn't nervous either.
Only the first person studies English.

readAndPick.es:
No vivo en Bogotá.
Yo sí.
options: The second person lives in Bogotá.

readAndPick.es: Tomás no trabaja los lunes. Vale tampoco.
options: Neither of them works on Mondays.

yourTurn.prompt: Your friend says: *Estoy tranquilo.* Say 'me too'.
Your friend says: *No tengo computadora.* Say 'me neither'.
yourTurn.why: A no-sentence takes *tampoco*. *Yo también* would mean you disagree.

yourTurn.prompt: Your friend says: *No hablo japonés.* Say you do.
yourTurn.why: To disagree with a no-sentence, say *sí*.

yourTurn.prompt: Your friend says: *Leo el correo los lunes.* Say you don't.
yourTurn.why: To disagree with a yes-sentence, say *no*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I don't work on Mondays either.
yourTurn.why: *Tampoco* goes in front of the verb, and then you don't need *no*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Vale cooks, and Tomás does too.
yourTurn.why: Just add the name and *también*: no verb needed.

yourTurn.answer: Yo también vivo en el centro.
yourTurn.why: *También* can go right before the verb.

pitfalls.wrong:
No tengo plan.
Yo no también.
pitfalls.why: There's no '*no también*' in Spanish. Agreeing with a no-sentence is *tampoco*.
*Yo también* after a no-sentence sounds like 'I do speak it'.

personal: Think of something you don't do on Mondays and something you do every week. Write each one, then answer yourself with *Yo también* or *Yo tampoco* as if you were your best friend.
